slot.brief: Two point charges fixed, find null point position where field is zero

stem: Charges $+16q$ and $-q$ are fixed on the $x$-axis at $x=-6$ cm and $x=18$ cm, respectively. The coordinate of the point where the electric field is zero is

verdicts.working: Between the charges, both fields point right, so they cannot cancel. To the right of both, set \(16/(x+6)^2=1/(x-18)^2\), giving \(4/(x+6)=1/(x-18)\) and \(x=26\,\text{cm}\).

working:
$x>18$ cm, so the fields oppose.
$$\dfrac{16}{(x+6)^2}=\dfrac{1}{(x-18)^2}$$
$$\dfrac{4}{x+6}=\dfrac{1}{x-18}\Rightarrow 4x-72=x+6\Rightarrow x=26\text{ cm}$$

Independent check: Between the charges, both fields point right, so they cannot cancel. To the right of both, set \(16/(x+6)^2=1/(x-18)^2\), giving \(4/(x+6)=1/(x-18)\) and \(x=26\,\text{cm}\).
